title: Route alias double-applying burst credits causing transient over-allow and billing mismatch
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Summary: Several customer incidents reported transient allowance spikes where requests routed via route aliases or fallback rules consumed burst credits twice, resulting in short windows of permissive enforcement and overstated billing. This ticket tracks investigation, root cause, and the implementation plan to fix duplication and ensure atomic credit accounting across routing transformations.

Background: Our policy engine applies burst credits at the enforcement point per (org,key,route) tuple. Recent changes introduced route alias resolution and a fast fallback routing path for Dedicated->Hosted fallback. Under certain race conditions both the canonical route and the aliased route enforcement path applied credit consumption, creating double-debits at enforcement time while only one token was intended to be consumed. The net effect observed: transient higher throughput (allowing more requests than configured), followed by a larger-than-expected meter emission leading to customer billing discrepancies and quota exhaustion downstream.

Why this matters: Customers relying on strict per-route quotas (and our enterprise billing reconciliation) saw unexplained overages and temporary quota misbehavior. This is a P1 customer-impact issue (high for affected orgs).
reproduction_steps: 1) Enable route aliasing for a route (e.g., route /v1/gen -> alias /gen-stable) and set a small burst credit window (e.g., 50 tokens, refill 10/s).
2) Configure a fallback routing rule that redirects to a hosted model variant when dedicated pool signals degraded capacity.
3) From a single API key, send concurrent request bursts (50-200 reqs) while toggling dedicated pool availability (simulate by marking a node unhealthy).
4) Observe enforcement logs: you'll see two enforcement evaluations for the same logical request in a ~10-30ms window and two debit events emitted to the meter pipeline for a subset of requests.
5) Confirm billing counter delta in /internal/meters API and quoter_state snapshots: debit_count increments by ~2x for affected requests.
investigation_notes: - Initial reports came from two enterprise customers (CS case #4728, #4812). Both showed same fingerprint: high concurrent bursts + alias usage.
- Reproduced locally with a stress harness. Intermittent: ~12% of requests in a burst triggered dual debit path.
- Trace correlation: requests that hit the fast fallback codepath first then canonical resolver would schedule a second enforcement call before the enforcement mutex released.

- Root logs: enforcement_id UUID different for both evaluations because route resolution mutated the enforcement key (alias -> canonical) between steps. Metering component treats enforcement_id as independent and emits two debit events.
- Race window narrowed to ~5-40ms based on concurrency and GC pauses on nodes handling route resolution caching.
- No evidence of persistent state corruption; problem is atomicity and idempotency of debit ops across routing transformations.
root_cause: When route alias resolution and fallback routing both trigger enforcement evaluation paths, the enforcement pipeline lacked a global idempotency key that represents the logical request (org,key,request_id,resolved_route_version). Because route resolution sometimes happens concurrently in two codepaths, both produced semantically distinct enforcement events which the meter ingestor accepted and charged. The policy engine's debit operation is not idempotent across logically-equivalent enforcement events when route identity changes mid-flight.
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce a deterministic enforcement id (enforcement_fingerprint) computed early in the request lifecycle and carried through routing decisions. This fingerprint will be used as an idempotency key for debit and meter emission.
2) Make debit operations idempotent at the meter ingestor: reject repeated debit attempts with the same enforcement_fingerprint.
3) Ensure route resolution is canonicalized before any enforcement call whenever possible; when not possible implement a short-lived in-memory dedupe for enforcement attempts per request.
4) Add unit/integration tests covering alias+fallback simultaneous paths and chaos tests that flip route resolution mid-request.
rollout_plan: Phase A (dev): implement enforcement_fingerprint generation in runtime and local idempotency in enforcement shim. Add unit/integration tests (branch feature flag).
Phase B (canary): enable idempotency checks in meter ingestor for 5% of traffic and monitor debit deltas and enforcement log dedupe rates.
Phase C (inc): if stable, increase to 50% then 100% traffic and remove the feature flag after 1 week with no regressions.
Emergency mitigation: if widespread billing drift observed, toggle a temporary enforcement atomic mutex to serialize enforcement for aliased routes (cost: latency degradation) while we ramp fix.
testing_plan: - Unit tests: enforcement_fingerprint deterministic across permutations of route aliasing and fallback resolution.
- Integration tests: stress harness that runs with varying concurrency, asserting debit_count == expected_count and no double-debits after fix.
- Chaos test: flip route cache state and node health during burst to verify idempotent behavior under race.
- Regression: run nightly billing-reconciliation job against synthetic workload to ensure meter parity.
monitoring_and_alerting: - New metric: enforcement_fingerprint_dedupe_rate (per org/route) — alerts if > 0.5% over baseline.
- Billing delta alert: daily reconciled_invoice_delta > $50 for an org triggers pager after fix rollout.
- Latency guardrail: if enforcement serialization fallback used, alert if p95 increases > 25%.
- Logs: add structured field enforcement_fingerprint to enforcement and meter logs for post-mortems.
follow_up_tasks: - ENG-76010: Update public billing docs to describe eventual consistency windows and what happened in this class of incidents.
- PM: coordinate with CS to identify affected customers and offer reconciliation/credits where applicable.
- Run a postmortem and update playbook for routing-related metering bugs.
- Remove temporary fallbacks and mutexes once idempotency is validated.
